Shower Tile Installation: If you are looking for professional shower tile installation near Middletown, you are in the right place, as we offer professional shower tile laying services. Installation begins with preparing the substrate and shower structure. Appropriate waterproofing systems are essential for walls and floors before tile installation to protect the underlying structure. Sheet membranes, waterproof boards, or liquid-applied membranes are used according to the method of installation. Depending on the waterproofing system, properly treat niches, benches, corners, seams, and plumbing fixtures. After waterproofing, measuring the shower area is essential to plan the layout. Reference lines help ensure proper cuts around showerheads, valves, drains, corners, benches, and other areas. There must be a sloped floor directed toward the drain. A thin-set mortar is used to prepare the surface, and tiles are installed with proper alignment and consistent joints. Accurate measurement is also important for plumbing openings. Grout is applied to the joints when the mortar is set, and excess grout is wiped off from the surface. Grout should not be taken as a substitute for the waterproofing system behind the tiles. Flexible sealant is used in areas where movement joints are present. The final stage of installation involves cleaning the tiles, removing excess grout, evaluating alignment, and inspecting plumbing fixtures, niches, and particularly drains.

That's a mistake. We will show you why you should always overthink your kitchen lighting. Must-know kitchen lighting design tips for your new kitchen start with one core principle: lighting does more work in a kitchen than in almost any other room. It supports prep, cooking, cleaning, and entertaining — often all at once. Get it wrong and even a beautifully designed luxury kitchen feels dim, flat, or frustrating to use. Why Kitchen Lighting Deserves More Thought Than Most Decisions Kitchen lighting affects how you see food, how safe the workspace feels, and how the room looks morning through evening. A single overhead fixture — the default in many new builds — creates shadows on countertops and leaves the edges of the room in gloom. Cooking in those conditions isn't just inconvenient. It can be a safety issue. Lighting also affects how the kitchen feels. A bright, evenly lit space reads as clean and functional. A kitchen with layered, dimmable light sources reads as warm and considered. The difference is rarely about budget — it's about planning.
